43.0.s.en: 1. Fear not, for I am with you:

43.0.0.en: 1 And now thus saith the LORD that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel: “Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine. 2 When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be scorched; neither shall the flame burn thee. 3 For I am the LORD thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour: I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee. 4 Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life. 5 Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; 6 I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth; 7 Even every one that is called by my name: for I have created him for my glory, I have formed him; yea, I have made him.”

43.0.1.en: He begins His speech thus: “And now thus” [1]; as though God wants to change the previous picture, the picture of the bitter captivity of sin, which robbed us of inner insight and of the ears of the soul, by presenting the riches of His saving promises and the abundance of His surpassing grace.

43.0.2.en: God wants us to turn our eyes away from our wretched state or from thinking about what sin has done in us, looking instead to the Redeemer and Savior, so that despair may not crush us but we may be filled with hope.

43.0.3.en: Now what is the role of the Redeemer who frees us from the captivity of sin?

43.0.4.en: a. God the Creator alone is able to renew creation: “And now thus saith the LORD that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee” [1].

43.0.5.en: When Arius denied the divinity of the Lord Christ, St. Athanasius the Apostolic concentrated in his reply to him on the fact that the divinity of the Lord is not a theoretical, philosophical doctrine but a matter that touches our very salvation. Our human nature had become utterly corrupt and needed the Creator to save our fallen nature and restore it to its origin, granting it His image and reforming it from corruption to incorruption; in Him humanity overcomes death and is re-created. There was urgent need for the Son of God, one with the Father and equal to Him in essence, to offer Himself as a sacrifice able to pay the debt of our sins and to fulfill divine justice and mercy at the same time. He is God, who overcomes Satan, not for His own sake but in the name of humanity and on its behalf. Finally, being true God, He restored to us our dignity, granting us sonship to the Father in Him by the Holy Spirit. Pope Athanasius says: [He became man that we might become gods], [and though there is one Son by nature, a true, only-begotten Son, we have become sons not by nature and truth but by His grace that calls us, and though we are men on earth, yet we have been called gods].

43.0.6.en: St. John Chrysostom says: [Because of love He took our flesh and had compassion on us; there is no other reason for His Incarnation]. God did not repay us for our many transgressions that we committed against Him despite His benefactions to us, but gave us His Son. He made Him sin for our sake... He let Him be condemned and die as one accursed. He who knew no sin He made as a sinner and as sin... He is like a king who sees a thief about to be executed, and sends his beloved only son, transferring upon him the very death and even the criminal’s fault! All this for the salvation of the guilty one, to raise him to great honor], [The Lord Christ paid more than we deserve, by as much as the ocean exceeds a drop of water].

43.0.7.en: By this we understand the prophetic words: “Thus saith the LORD that created thee... Fear not: for I have redeemed thee” [1].

43.0.8.en: b. Personal care on the part of the Savior toward man; God did not create man as one being among billions of beings that He brought into existence, but gave him special care as a creature beloved to Him; He knows man by name, and calls him and redeems him to be His, that is, that man may enjoy union with Him.

43.0.9.en: How beautiful is the voice of the Redeemer when He speaks intimately to every man, saying:

43.0.10.en: “Fear not: for I have redeemed thee.

43.0.11.en: I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine” [1].

43.0.12.en: The secret of redemption lies in God’s surpassing love: He wants me for Himself, and He is mine... He knows me by name and calls me to enter with Him into a unique relationship of love. He asks nothing of me but asks my being and my heart and my love, and I do not ask His gifts but His person and His Holy Spirit and His love! It is as though God here comes forward as Creator and Savior and a personal Bridegroom to me.

43.0.13.en: * My God... when I contemplate in my conscience, I see You always looking toward me, and attending to me day and night with great effort, as though there were no creature in heaven or on earth but me.

43.0.14.en: * Your eyes are drawn toward the steps of men...

43.0.15.en: Since You care for all Your creation, You deprive none of the work of Your hands of the abundance of Your love!

43.0.16.en: You Yourself care for my steps and my ways night and day, You watch over my care, You observe all my paths, You do not cease to care for me, so that I could say that You forget heaven and earth and what is in them, concentrating Your care on me, so that You seem as one who cares for no creature but me!

43.0.17.en: * You watch over me as though You had forgotten all creation! You give me Your gifts as though I alone were the object of Your love!

43.0.18.en: * There is never anything that You do not know... my thoughts, my purposes, my joys and my works... none of this is not laid before Your eternal care!

43.1.0.en: St. Augustine c. God the Savior is the secret of our victory; as long as He is with us the waters of this world do not overwhelm us nor do the fires of lusts burn us: “When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be scorched; neither shall the flame burn thee” [2].

43.1.1.en: A wonderful picture of the Savior’s work: He gives us Himself, so death with all its means and ways cannot swallow us... We bear our Christ, “the Resurrection” (Jn 11:25), within us, and we live the risen life that overcomes death.

43.1.2.en: If we face the waters of the love of the world that drown the soul and kill it, and the flame of the fire of lust that destroys it, the Savior has given us His Holy Spirit through the waters of Baptism, in which we renounce Satan and all his hosts and all his works and bruise his head under our feet; He gave us His Holy, fiery Spirit as on the day of Pentecost, who burns up sin and scatters its deadly flame.

43.1.3.en: Perhaps the prophet Isaiah here reminds his people of God’s work with their fathers at their exodus from Egypt. By the cross He gave them victory over the waters of the Sea of Suph (by means of the rod), and also victory over the fiery serpents (by the bronze serpent). God who worked in ancient times works in the second exodus from the Babylonian captivity, and these two exoduses are a type of the greatest exodus that the Savior accomplishes by His cross in the lives of His believers.

43.1.4.en: * Can you resist Satan, O you unfaithful ones, unless you have the shield of faith? For by it you are able to quench his darts...!

43.1.5.en: Do you perhaps justify yourself since sin has reigned over your body? And how can you glorify God in your body, when He is the One who redeemed you with His pure blood?!

43.2.0.en: St. Anba Shenouda, Archimandrite d. The Savior pays the price: the early Church looked to the cross as the payment of the debt that we owed to the Father, and as an acquiring of us from the hand of the devil, who bought us as slaves to himself, so the Lord paid His blood as the price for this for our freedom. This is the work of the holy Savior, who wants to sanctify us by His blood and free us from the slavery of the devil; therefore He says: “For I am the LORD thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour: I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee” [3].

43.2.1.en: Egypt with its Pharaoh, which represented one of the two great powers at that time (Egypt and Assyria; then Egypt and Babylon...), does not support God’s people nor protect them but occupies a position of weakness... As for Cush and Seba, they were known for their wealth. It is as though God is the One who redeems and saves, being the Holy One, and not Pharaoh with his might nor Cush and Seba with their riches and resources.

43.2.2.en: The Lord bought us not with gold or silver but with His precious blood, to make us kings and priests:

43.2.3.en: “For thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation; and hast made us unto our God kings and priests” (Rev 5:9-10).

43.2.4.en: “For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your bodies and in your spirits, which are God’s” (1 Cor 6:20).

43.2.5.en: “Ye are bought with a price; be not ye the servants of men” (1 Cor 7:23).

43.2.6.en: “Knowing that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers; but with the precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot, even the blood of Christ” (1 Pet 1:18-19).

43.2.7.en: * You were bought with a price, that is, with blood. You have been removed from the empire of the flesh so that you may glorify the Lord in your bodies.

43.2.8.en: Tertullian * Let no one think that a different price was paid for him because of his wealth; for wealth in the Church is wealth in faith; for the believer has the whole world of wealth. What wonder is this if the believer possesses the inheritance of Christ, which is more precious than the world.

43.3.0.en: St. Ambrose e. The Savior restores to us our glory and our unity: often many despaired during the captivity of the possibility of returning to their land because of the length of their stay in it, but God the Savior reassures His children, saying: “Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth; even every one that is called by my name: for I have created him for my glory, I have formed him; yea, I have made him” [5-7].

43.3.1.en: It is noticed in this chapter that God speaks of Himself as “I” no fewer than 36 times, so that it has been called the chapter of “the divine Self” or “the divine I,” and the same occurs in the forty-fifth chapter 31 times... What does this mean? If the work of sin is man’s encapsulation in the “I,” so that he finds in himself a center for the world and for others, wanting to enjoy bodily pleasures or honor for his own account in pride and selfishness, then our Christ on the contrary offers His Self, which is “Love,” that we may possess Him. When He calls to us not to fear, and when He calls us by name, and affirms His care for us wherever we are and whatever trials come upon us, and when He offers us His promises to gather us from the ends of the inhabited world to embrace us to Himself... in all this He seeks not what is for Himself but what is ours. He grants us His presence that we may possess Him. Therefore from time to time He says “I am with thee,” and that He is ours, our eternal portion.

43.3.2.en: The glory of God’s name and His honor are declared in His practical, self-giving love, in the giving of Himself to His creation.

43.4.0.en: 8 Bring forth the blind people that have eyes, and the deaf that have ears. 9 “Gather together, O all ye nations, and let the tribes be assembled: who among them can declare this, and shew us former things? let them bring forth their witnesses, that they may be justified: or let them hear, and say, It is truth. 10 Ye are my witnesses, saith the LORD, and my servant whom I have chosen: that ye may know and believe me, and understand that I am he: before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me. 11 I, even I, am the LORD; and beside me there is no saviour. 12 I have declared, and have saved, and I have shewed, and there is no stranger among you: and ye are my witnesses, saith the LORD, and I am God. 13 Also from this day I am he; and there is none that can deliver out of my hand: I will work, and who shall turn it back?”

43.4.2.en: He offers Himself as light to us, opening our senses to see His glories in us and His heavenly Kingdom revealed within us, and opens our ears to hear His divine voice and to understand the aim of His commandment, so that we have the ears of children who know their father’s voice and even the movement of his feet... This is what He meant by saying: “Bring forth the blind people that have eyes, and the deaf that have ears” [8].

43.4.3.en: This is the role of God our Savior in our inner life, where He renews our nature in the waters of Baptism by His Holy Spirit to grant us the new man able to enjoy divine fellowship.

43.5.0.en: Through this experience we bear witness to others, and the Church calls for a general assembly of the nations [9-13] to get to know the Savior and to confirm the fulfillment of what He had promised before through His prophets across the generations before His coming.

43.5.1.en: “Gather together, O all ye nations, and let the tribes be assembled: who among them can declare this, and shew us former things? let them bring forth their witnesses, that they may be justified: or let them hear, and say, It is truth. Ye are my witnesses, saith the LORD, and my servant whom I have chosen: that ye may know and believe me, and understand that I am he: before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me. I, even I, am the LORD; and beside me there is no saviour...” [9-11].

43.5.2.en: God requires those who have enjoyed the new insight and the new spiritual ears to call the nations and tribes to enter with them into a practical dialogue through what they live. In this dialogue they declare the following:

43.5.3.en: a. Let them ask the nations whether they have earlier clear and sure prophecies concerning the future (Isa 41:22); but as for us, we have received prophecies not about the victory of Cush over Babylon to rescue the ancient people of God, but about the Messiah, the chosen Servant. We received prophecies about His person and His works and His mission; we knew that He would be born of a virgin, and we knew the time of His birth and its place, and about His works with His people and the offering of Himself as a unique sacrifice of love, etc... So what the prophets uttered concerned the unique, eternal Lord before whom no god was formed and after whom there shall be none... and as He says: “I am the first, and I am the last” (Isa 44:6).

43.5.4.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that Satan is able to imitate miracles [but prophecy is the special work of God, which the demons cannot imitate, though they struggle mightily for it].

43.5.5.en: In His love for mankind God gave the prophets these prophecies, and spoke through the tongue of His holy men and inspired the divine Word, and He still works in us by granting us the knowledge of these divine mysteries. And as Irenaeus says: [It is impossible for us, without God, to come to the knowledge of God, who teaches men through His Word].

43.6.0.en: b. Besides the prophecy that centered on the coming of the Savior... Holy Scripture affirms that God alone is the Savior: “I, even I, am the LORD; and beside me there is no saviour” [11]. God the Creator, in His jealousy for His beloved man, entrusts his salvation to no one but shepherds His people Himself and lays down His life for them: “the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep” (Jn 10:11). He created, and He is the One who renews creation and saves it!

43.6.1.en: In His repetition of “I, even I, am the LORD” is an affirmation that the One who offers salvation is the Lord Himself, the First and the Last, declaring His divine love through His saving knowledge!

43.6.2.en: * Being “the Life,” He died that we might live; being “the Word,” He became flesh that He might teach the flesh in the Word.

43.6.3.en: * He is the Word of God and His power and His wisdom, as Solomon testifies concerning wisdom that it is “the One, she can do all things, and remaining in herself, she maketh all things new, and passing into holy souls, she formeth friends of God, and prophets” (Wis 7:27).

43.7.0.en: 14 Thus saith the LORD, your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “For your sake I have sent to Babylon, and have cast down all the bars, and the Chaldeans in the ships of their singing. 15 I am the LORD, your Holy One, the creator of Israel, your King.

43.7.1.en: God, who allowed the discipline of His people by the Babylonian captivity, now, out of His love for His people, allows the fall of Babylon. He speaks in the past tense to assure His hearers that what will happen is an actual fact that must be accomplished.

43.7.2.en: The text has come differently from one translation to another while the meaning remains constant:

43.7.3.en: “Thus saith the LORD, your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I have sent to Babylon, and cast the bars upon it (brought down its nobles), and the Chaldeans in the ships of their singing (their cry in their ships)” [14].

43.7.4.en: Here God appears as the commander of the hostile armies, sending Media and Persia to Babylon, and there He casts terror into the hearts of its inhabitants so that they flee quickly.

43.7.5.en: The Hebrew word barichim was translated “nobles,” and in Arabic “bars,” and the English has used “nobles” because they protect the city like bars for it.

43.7.6.en: Many of the rich fled to their ships that were moored in the Euphrates and the Tigris. Babylon had no seagoing ships, but the rich went out to their pleasure boats, therefore it was said “ships of their singing,” because they were accustomed to use them during their trips full of mirth. And when they found in them no possibility of salvation, their songs turned into cries and bitterness.

43.8.0.en: In [15] God is called by three titles: Jehovah, your Savior, the Holy One of Israel, through which He reveals the role of God as leader of His people or His Church; He is the God unchanging in His love and His power, able to grant victory over the enemy of good; He is the Savior who in His love offers the unique sacrifice of salvation; and He is the Holy One who renews the creation of His believers and sanctifies them to reign with Him eternally.

43.8.1.en: Perhaps by these three titles He intended that salvation and sanctification are at the very heart of the work of God as One who loves His weak creation and longs to renew it in Himself.

43.9.0.en: 16 Thus saith the LORD, which maketh a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters; 17 Which bringeth forth the chariot and horse, the army and the power; they shall lie down together, they shall not rise: they are extinct, they are quenched as tow. 18 “Remember ye not the former things, neither consider the things of old. 19 Behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall ye not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert. 20 The beast of the field shall honour me, the wolves and the daughters of the ostrich: because I have made waters in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen. 21 This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise.

43.9.1.en: God, who saves His people, had previously given them salvation by the hands of Moses to free them from the slavery of Pharaoh; and here He brings them out of the Babylonian captivity as in a new exodus, and He remains continually bringing them out from the captivity of sin to the freedom of the glory of the children of God, setting them forth, as it were, from the works of the old man to the continual enjoyment of the works of the new, inner man.

43.9.2.en: “Thus saith the LORD, which maketh a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters; which bringeth forth the chariot and horse, the army and the power; they shall lie down together, they shall not rise: they are extinct, they are quenched as tow” [16-17].

43.9.3.en: He saved them from the power of Pharaoh by their crossing the Sea of Suph, cutting off every possibility of Pharaoh’s rising against them again. He likened Pharaoh’s sudden and swift destruction to a wick that was quenched and does not blaze again; with the same power God saves them from the hand of Babylon also.

43.10.0.en: This salvation that was accomplished against Pharaoh and also against Babylon must be accomplished against the works of the old man (Col 3:9), so the prophet continues his speech, saying: “Remember ye not the former things, neither consider the things of old; behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall ye not know it?! I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert” [18-19]. He wants us not only to put off the old man with his works but to forget him completely and no longer remember him or ponder him, lest we despair and be shattered, but rather be occupied with the new life that springs forth in us. He makes a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert. What is this way but the Lord Christ Himself, who says: “I am the way” (Jn 14:6), who arose in the midst of us, the barren wilderness, and dwells in our hearts to enter with us into His Kingdom?! And what are these rivers but the springs of the Holy Spirit bursting forth within us, the desert without inhabitant, so that our desolate heart is turned into a dwelling of the Holy God?! It is as though the secret of our renewal is the indwelling of the Lord Christ in us and the coming of His Holy Spirit in our inner depths.

43.11.0.en: God affirms the opening of the door of faith before the Gentiles to acquire a new people, who know inner joy and praise, saying: “The beast of the field shall honour me, the wolves and the daughters of the ostrich: because I have made waters in the wilderness, rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen. This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise” [20-21]. He likens the Gentiles to the wild beasts that live in the wilderness, because of the extreme violence that marked them, and because they lived as in a wilderness with no promises among them, no covenants, no divine law, etc... in a state of extreme desolation. They were likened also to the daughters of the ostrich, a symbol of folly and lack of understanding because of their worship of idols and their practicing of abominations as a pious religious act. These, who were known for cruelty and folly, who lived in a barren wilderness, have come to enjoy the water of the rivers of the Holy Spirit to drink and be satisfied, and to receive membership in the chosen people of God. Thus their nature is changed through the work of the Holy Trinity in them, and their heart is opened to joy and their tongue to praise.

43.12.0.en: How beautiful is the divine phrase: “This people have I formed for myself!” [21] We have become His, the Lord’s portion, as He is ours, our portion!

43.13.0.en: 22 “And thou hast not called upon me, O Jacob, that thou shouldest weary thyself for me, O Israel. 23 Thou hast not brought me the sheep of thy burnt offerings; neither hast thou honoured me with thy sacrifices. I have not caused thee to serve with an offering, nor wearied thee with incense. 24 Thou hast bought me no sweet cane with silver, neither hast thou satisfied me with the fat of thy sacrifices: but thou hast made me to serve with thy sins, thou hast wearied me with thine iniquities. 25 I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake, and I will not remember thy sins.” 26 “Put me in remembrance: let us plead together: declare thou, that thou mayest be justified. 27 Thy first father hath sinned, and thy mediators have transgressed against me. 28 Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary, and have given Jacob to the curse, and Israel to reproaches.”

43.13.1.en: God offers His saving works freely to humanity, but there are some obstacles that hindered God’s purposes with the ancient people who refused to believe in the Savior; these obstacles are:

43.13.2.en: a. Not praying: “And thou hast not called upon me, O Jacob, that thou shouldest weary thyself for me, O Israel” [22]. For prayer is the secret of our enjoyment of God’s work, and as Father Martyrius says: [Prayer does what it wishes as God can! It issues commands on earth that they may have their effect in heaven].

43.14.0.en: b. Ignoring God even in small matters: “Thou hast not brought me the sheep of thy burnt offerings; neither hast thou honoured me with thy sacrifices. I have not caused thee to serve with an offering, nor wearied thee with incense. Thou hast bought me no sweet cane with silver, neither hast thou satisfied me with the fat of thy sacrifices” [23-24].

43.14.1.en: When God brought His people out of Egypt He was not in need of their offerings and animal sacrifices, but sought their hearts, longing to draw them near to Himself as His own people, while the sacrifices were types of the sacrifice of Christ and a sign of love for Him... He was waiting for them to offer their hearts with their burnt offerings and sacrifices and incense, etc...

43.14.2.en: * When He indicates that He did not lead them out of Egypt that they might offer Him sacrifice but that they might forget the worship of idols of the Egyptians so that they might hear the voice of the Lord, which was for them salvation and glory (Jer 7:21).

43.15.0.en: St. Irenaeus c. Preoccupation with bodily pleasures and worldly lusts: “but thou hast made me to serve with thy sins, thou hast wearied me with thine iniquities” [24]. Instead of honoring the Lord by offering the heart as a burnt sacrifice together with practicing worship, the people turned to selfishness and entanglement with temporal things, so they exploited God’s love and care and gifts for the sake of the “I.”

43.15.1.en: We often misuse the gifts of God, such as emotions, impulses and talents; we use them not for the sake of the Kingdom of God and the edification of the community but to practice evil.

43.16.0.en: Despite the evil we have reached, God remains waiting for our repentance and our confession of our sins that He may forgive them for us for the sake of His holy name and His surpassing love, assuring us: “I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake, and I will not remember thy sins; put me in remembrance: let us plead together: declare thou, that thou mayest be justified” [25-26].

43.16.1.en: * The first way of repentance is our condemnation of sins.

43.16.2.en: * He asks this of us (the confession of our sins) that we may intensify our love toward Him.

43.16.3.en: * He who practices repentance after he sins deserves not grief over him but congratulation, as he passes over to the choir of the righteous.

43.17.0.en: * Let nothing confuse you but rise up to the highest heavens themselves. Sigh bitterly and offer a sacrifice of confession, for it was said, “Declare thou first thy transgressions, that thou mayest be justified” [26] (the Septuagint); offer the sacrifice of a contrite heart. For these sacrifices are not turned into ashes, nor become smoke, nor are dissipated in the air. They need no wood and fire but a heart repentant within. This is the wood and the fire that burn without destroying, for he who prays fervently is burned but not consumed, but becomes like gold tried by fire that it may increase in splendor.

43.17.1.en: St. John Chrysostom Thus it befits us to remember our sins and confess them so that they may be forgiven... Then we ought to remember God’s work with us and glorify Him instead of thinking of the sins...

43.17.2.en: * How do we forget the evil that is coming upon us? By the remembrance of good things, and by remembering God. For if we remember God continually we cannot remember these things also.

43.18.0.en: St. John Chrysostom We must not be ashamed of confessing sins, for our first fathers sinned before us, foremost among them Adam the first: “Thy first father hath sinned, and thy mediators have transgressed against me” [27]. The majority of the Fathers of the Church, and also the rabbis, see that it means all humanity represented in Adam our first father, and some interpret it in the light of what is stated in (Ezek 16:3) “thy father was an Amorite.” Some saw that it is the chief father Urijah as the high priest who led the people to the worship of idols in the days of Ahaz (2 Kgs 16:10-16), and some saw that it means the kings and high priests, that is, the civil and religious leaders together leading the people to disobedience.

43.19.0.en: The fruit of sins and disobedience is “the curse” and the loss of honor, for it was said: “I have given Jacob to the curse, and Israel to reproaches” [28].
